known_limitations: Version-number matching ONLY. This does not verify that a repo file's SQL is byte-identical to what schema_migrations recorded as having run. PR #1471's own reconciliation found at least 3 of 5 filed sets were NOT byte-identical to their pre-apply drafts (gh1070 most notably: the draft says NOT APPLIED, what ran was shorter and different). This manifest cannot and does not catch that class of drift -- it only tracks presence of a version, not correctness of its content.

'repo_file_no_applied' conflates two different things this manifest does not distinguish: (a) genuinely abandoned drafts (e.g. c4_contractor_pitch_bands, confirmed not-live in PR #1471), and (b) a brand-new migration mid-flight between being filed and being auto-run post-merge (D-221 Path A: 'GitHub PR -> merge -> Supabase migration auto-run', per CLAUDE.md). The PR gate deliberately does NOT fail on growth in this direction for exactly that reason -- see scripts/migrations-reconciliation-check.py's compute_verdict docstring.

This is a point-in-time snapshot (2026-09-01T19:16:46Z, after PR #1471 and #1475 merged to main). It does not match the CTO's 104/28 figure quoted the same day at 13:03Z -- v115/gh1304 and gh1425 applied and their repo files landed in between. That is expected: this is a fresh live measurement per this dispatch's own instructions, not a copy of a number quoted in the work order.

The 13 versions with both a forward and a rollback (or pre-flight doc) filed directly into supabase/migrations/ (not a drafts subdirectory) are a recurrence of the defect PR #385 previously fixed, independently flagged in a prior gh-1438 dispatch's evidence comment (gh1041, gh1245x2, gh1253 restamp, gh1387, gh1425, plus v113/v113b/v114/v115/v116 here). NOT fixed by this dispatch -- out of scope by the CTO's ruling ('do not backfill'). The version-level check below is unaffected by it (both files share one version and the version either has a file or it doesn't), but a human reading supabase/migrations/ should not assume every *_rollback.sql there is unreachable dead weight -- some document what forward.sql undoes and both are load-bearing history.

THE MECHANISM GAP THIS MANIFEST DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY: a migration applied directly to production outside any PR (via apply_migration through the Supabase MCP or dashboard, with no file ever committed to this repo) is invisible to a per-PR repo-diff check by construction -- no file changed, so there is no diff, so there is no signal for the CI gate to act on. That is the exact leak the CTO's ruling names ('gh1410_claims_measurement_shape made it 110 last night, by exactly the leak this issue names'). This dispatch's CI check (scripts/migrations-reconciliation-check.py) catches the one widening vector fully visible in a PR diff -- deletion of a file that documents an already-applied, already-documented migration -- and does not attempt to catch the out-of-band leak, which needs a live query against production and cannot honestly be attributed to any single PR (a scheduled, non-blocking alarm job, per this repo's own edge-function-drift.yml precedent, would be the mechanism for that; not built in this dispatch -- flagged as a follow-up, not silently dropped).
